operations.comment: ; Validated iNES header defines 32 KiB PRG, 32 KiB CHR, mapper 3 and horizontal mirroring.
; iNES: 2 x 16 KiB PRG, 4 x 8 KiB CHR, mapper 3, horizontal mirroring, no trainer/battery.
; Header is cartridge metadata, not executable CPU or PPU storage.
; Fixed PRG entry stub forwards to cold reset. CNROM changes CHR only; CPU slots retain physical banks [0,1,2,3].
; Fixed PRG entry stub forwards to the vblank interrupt handler.

; Palette-sized values; pointer groups and repeated width/height/tile records, recognizable mission briefing strings; code resumes at $85F4. Consumers include $AD17/$DF8F tile/display pointers and $B311 mission arrays. Checked full hex and neighboring control-flow, no conflicting fetched starts. Composite generic data; precise record schemas remain unresolved.
; Fixed CPU view $8006..$85F3; source bytes remain in the local image asset.

; Wait for NMI, build queued sprites, then advance palette transitions, mission outcome tests, HUD work and projected objects. The simulation itself runs in NMI. Rendering work is spread across an eight-step phase to bound per-frame updates.
; Save four palette triplets and two accent colors before the transition begins.
; State $FE moves colors toward the dark range once every four phase ticks; the helper counts unfinished channels.
; State $FD installs dark colors and resets selected display motion. Timed states then reach the restoration phase.
; Restore saved hues with a dark luminance; later steps restore the saved full values.
; Every eighth phase tick, move each color toward its saved value. Advance only when all channels have converged.
; A pending display refresh rebuilds the mission-specific foreground. Fuel drains on a slower divider and can raise the low-fuel alert.
; Pause masks gameplay controls. Check special mission completion, fuel exhaustion and damage limit before scheduling result initialization.
; Block for a bounded 60-step color flash with randomized palette choices and periodic sound, then mark mission failure.
; Set failure, stop effects, clear the mission submode and enter the result screen through the main initializer pointer.
; Select two three-tile readouts from the aiming/range parameter; append address, count and payload to the PPU queue.
; Sample the wrapped heading scale around the current heading and compose the HUD's small numeric/tick display.
; Update the two numeric mission counters, target readout or alert/resource panel according to the frame work phase.
; Resolve the selected object's text pointer and convert seven characters to HUD tiles. No target produces blank numeric tiles.
; Negative alert values request new text; positive values count down, with periodic sound near the start. Idle frames draw resource counters.
; Apply the pending direction inversion, compute target-relative decimal coordinates and project visible objects. A separate short-lived sprite effect uses its own countdown.
; Refresh direct OAM entries for the moving HUD particles and projectile indicators after queued scene work.
; Negative submodes drive the foreground sequence. Stream progress selects palette records, individual tiles or vertical tile columns; the normal mission returns immediately.
; Use the mission's foreground type to load a five-byte palette record, then advance submode.
; While waiting for a stream marker, sample every eighth progress step and queue a single tile from the selected foreground column.
; Use left/right input and stream progress to build a short terminated column update. These are PPU addresses and tile bytes, not CPU pointers.
; Resolve the current mission type and fill the foreground column transfer record.

; Inspect the player's occupancy cell, create up to two nearby objects, take a stable coordinate snapshot, then project and depth-sort active objects. Special negative cell values request contacts or the foreground sequence; their exact gameplay identities remain tentative.
; Enable the music driver, stop active effects and select song 1. Also used by completion/contact paths.
; Decode the cell's type/count into one of two free even-index object slots. Seed decimal coordinates around the current cell and clear motion/AI accumulators.
; Copy player and object coordinate pairs into work RAM. Restart the snapshot if NMI changed coordinates during the copy.
; Walk even-index slots from 8 down to 0. Compute wrapped decimal deltas on three axes; reject distant objects before the expensive perspective transform.
; Resolve the selected sprite's half extents and test its projected rectangle against the reticle. A hit stores the one-based object slot and scale.
; Destroyed objects expire after a scale-dependent delay. Remove their occupancy count and release the active slot when the delay ends.
; Clear visibility and auxiliary projected positions. Close-range slots additionally release their world coordinates and screen smoothing history.
; Convert A to decimal digit tiles, blank the leading zero, append both tiles at the requested HUD row.
; Saturate the damage counter at six, request a warning when crossing four and trigger the palette/shake response.
; Select the mission's background transfer through the mission lookup and perform it with rendering protected.
; Copy three mission-specific colors into the palette and return the next two accent values in A/Y.
; Three small numeric constants 08,08,16, bounded by returns and next routine. Indexed display context inspected; generic data without asserting exact meaning.
; Fixed CPU view $90CA..$90CC; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; SpawnHeightOffsets ($90CA): Two fixed low-byte height offsets used for object type one.

; Ease the reference X toward the left/right control target, then compute signed fractional velocities for half of the ten particle slots each phase. The eight-step quotient loop approximates direction without multiplication.
; A is current color; FadeTarget is saved color. Lower luminance by $10 until at/below target, then clamp; count channels still moving in FadePending.
; Raise low color values by $10 toward the dark threshold $20 and count unfinished channels. NES palette numbering makes the apparent direction counterintuitive.
; Select a source column using mission type Y and progress/8. Read four tiles at stride $20 and append an $FF terminator for the NMI column writer.

; Repeated bounded numeric runs, mission flags at $91E9 indexed by mission at $87D4, and interleaved HUD phrase character data. Noninstruction patterns inspected through next code boundary; exact text interleave remains unresolved.
; Fixed CPU view $91DF..$9315; source bytes remain in the local image asset.

; MissionForegroundTypes ($91E9): Ten mission-indexed foreground types/flags. Negative values select the special completion path.
; MissionInitialObjectives ($91F3): Ten mission-indexed initial objective counts.
; MissionAccentColors ($91FD): Palette selections addressed through MissionBackgroundSelectors.
; MissionBackgroundStripIndices ($9202): Background-strip selector for each mission palette choice.
; InitialParticleX ($9221): Ten fixed particle X positions, overriding randomized spawn positions at mission start.
; InitialParticleY ($922B): Ten fixed particle Y positions.
; DamageLampTiles ($9235): Three-byte tile groups selected by damage count and blink state.
; MissionOamTemplate ($924A): Twelve bytes copied into cockpit OAM during mission initialization.
; TrackStripPointersLo ($927A): Low-byte bases for the two animated six-tile track strips.
; TrackStripPointersHi ($927C): High-byte bases for the track-strip pointers.
; SpeedIndicatorAttributes ($927E): Speed-indexed sprite attributes; reverse mode selects the last entry.
; SpeedIndicatorTiles ($928C): Speed-indexed sprite tile values.
; SpeedIndicatorX0 ($929A): Speed-indexed first sprite horizontal offset.
; SpeedIndicatorX1 ($92A8): Speed-indexed second sprite horizontal offset.
; SpeedIndicatorY0 ($92B6): Speed-indexed first sprite Y values.
; SpeedIndicatorY1 ($92C4): Speed-indexed second sprite Y values.
; TargetTextPointersLo ($92D2): Low-byte pointer list for the target HUD text.
; TargetTextPointersHi ($92DF): High-byte pointer list for target HUD text.
; Walk seven unpacked decimal score digits, suppress leading zeroes and append the completed HUD run.
; A=count, X=column, HudRow=row. Compute $2000+row*32+column and copy tiles from the scratch row into the PPU queue; X becomes the updated queue tail.
; Copy the fixed 32-byte palette into palette RAM.
; Busy-wait until the NMI simulation tick changes. This is distinct from the general descending vblank counter.

; Repeated structured object-position pairs terminated by zero, followed by little-endian mission pointers $9479 indexed by $ADC4 and finite mission placement counts $948D consumed by $ADF7. Leading $9390-$9396 delay routine excluded; composite generic data without claiming every subrecord schema.
; Fixed CPU view $9397..$94A0; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; MissionPlacementPointers ($9479): Ten little-endian pointers to zero-terminated (cell value,index) placement pairs.
; MissionRandomPlacementCounts ($948D): Two ten-mission groups of randomized occupancy counts.
; Select blank tiles for the 16-character alert transfer; shares the queue builder with the visible-alert entry.
; Carry chooses visible versus blank alert text; A indexes the alert string. Convert sixteen characters and queue them at nametable $234D.

; Human-readable attack/mission/fuel/damage/mine messages followed by repeated small constants. At $9526..$952B values explicitly initialize state at $AE6A; full noninstruction text and adjacent numeric patterns inspected.
; Fixed CPU view $94D6..$9533; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; HudAlertCharacters ($94D6): Fixed-width alert text converted by HudCharacterToTile. Alert offsets select sixteen-character windows.
; PlayerInitialCoordinates ($9526): Six bytes copied into player decimal X/height/Z pairs.
; ObjectRetireSpriteVariants ($952C): Retirement-counter indexed sprite values used by projection.
; Set signed pixel step -1 and update eligible HUD particles through the shared depth-band motion logic.
; Set signed pixel step +1. Four accumulators decide which depth bands move; inactive particles are skipped.
; Preserve A/X/Y, convert A into three decimal tiles and suppress leading zeroes before restoring registers. Uses the circular HUD scratch row.
; Write tile A at HudColumn, advance the column modulo 32, and preserve A/Y for callers composing a run.
; Increment the scratch-row column with wrap at 32 tiles.
; Y holds two packed decimal digits, A the hundreds component. Expand tens by repeated addition and hundreds into a 16-bit binary result in Work0/Work1.
; Convert A using decimal powers-of-two and software BCD addition. Return hundreds/tens/ones as tile indices in A/X/Y, with digit zero represented by tile 8.
; Save A/X/Y in dedicated scratch bytes used by the numeric HUD formatter; this helper is not reentrant.
; Restore the numeric formatter's saved A/X/Y.
; Append projected scale, sprite variant, position, attribute and object index to parallel five-entry sort arrays. Caller has already bounded the number of candidates.
; Repeatedly choose the largest unprocessed scale and draw it, providing painter ordering. Some articulated variants add an offset component before or after the main sprite.
; Load the selected sorted entry's center and pass its variant to the attribute composer.
; Separate variant mirror bit, tint and priority behind the horizon; submit the resulting metasprite to the scene queue.
; Repeated zero/one flags and coordinate/tile-like constants between accepted routines. Full byte pattern inspected with neighboring indexed consumers; generic data, exact subfields unresolved.
; Fixed CPU view $97A2..$97A9; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; ObjectGraphicSetIndices ($97A2): Object type to sprite-table group selector.
; ObjectSpritePointersLo ($97A6): Low-byte sprite pointer-table roots.
; ObjectSpritePointersHi ($97A8): High-byte sprite pointer-table roots.
; Return Y=(player Z high nibble)*8+(player X high nibble), indexing the 8x8 occupancy map.
; Return Y=(A high nibble)*8+(X high nibble). Used to move occupancy counts between cells.
; 64-byte ascending 00..63 packed-BCD sequence; full extent inspected between code regions. Static lookup data, natural access unresolved.
; Fixed CPU view $97CB..$980A; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; MotionMagnitudeExpansion ($97CB): Magnitude expansion used when a shifted motion operand crosses a byte; exact original numerical generator unresolved.
; Classify signed object-relative X/Z into one of eight octants in Y, using a small dead zone of 50 binary units.
; Normalize the decimal delta in A:Work0 into a wrapped shortest magnitude and sign. Return the pair in A/Y and preserve the direction in Work2 bit 7.
; Repeated flags and smooth coordinate constants. $98C6 consumed at $8E01, mission-indexed $98D2/$98DC/$98E6 consumed at $F376/$F30E/$F304. Full boundaries and non-code patterns inspected.
; Fixed CPU view $98BE..$98EF; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; ObjectMotionScale ($98BE): Type-indexed velocity scaling shift counts.
; ObjectInitialHealth ($98C6): Object type to initial hit-point value.
; MissionEvasionProbability ($98D2): Mission-indexed random threshold in the evasive AI path.
; MissionAiRangeLo ($98DC): Low-byte mission-indexed near-range threshold.
; MissionAiRangeHi ($98E6): High-byte mission-indexed near-range threshold.
; Write the four resource values as separate three-digit HUD rows.
; Format A at column 26 and queue a three-tile row.
; Map space, dash, digits and lower-case ASCII letters to the compact HUD font's tile numbers.

; Order the absolute X/Z magnitudes, divide the smaller by the larger, binary-search the paired angle thresholds and round to the nearest sample. Fold signs/octants and subtract the player heading into an eight-sector relative bearing.
; Sixteen restoring-division steps form the ratio used by the angle lookup. Coordinate signs are retained separately.
; Maintain lower/upper lookup indices and bisect until the adjacent threshold brackets the quotient.
; Compare the remainder against half the next table interval, then fold octants and signs into a wrapped angle.
; Replace the angle with $0200-angle; shared by swapped-axis and opposite-sign cases.

; Palette-format values in 0..$3F with repeated universal-background $0F entries and four-byte grouping. Full interval lies between graphics routines; supported generic graphics data, precise palette selection unresolved.
; Fixed CPU view $9AD9..$9B18; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; MissionPaletteColors ($9AE1): 32-byte palette copied at mission initialization.
; ObjectPaletteTriplets ($9B01): Palette triplets selected from projected object type/variant.
; For each axis, retain the previous screen position on a direction reversal, then allow movement after the small hysteresis counter. Preserve caller X/Y.

; First 256-byte smooth monotonic quantized values indexed at $9B9C by $9F02; subsequent repeated coordinate/tile runs indexed at $9CAE/$9CBA/$9CC2 by $8DD7/$9720/$9749. Checked entire range and code boundaries; generic composite data, no claim of exact generator.
; Fixed CPU view $9B9C..$9E67; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; ProjectionDivisors ($9B9C): 256-entry quantized perspective divisor lookup; indexed by folded bearing. Exact original generator remains unresolved.
; CockpitAnchorOam ($9C9C): Four-byte OAM anchor used to recognize the cockpit raster split.
; SpriteDirectionBits ($9C9F): Direction-dependent sprite bit masks; this address also overlaps the cockpit anchor's X byte.
; SpriteMirrorBits ($9CA5): Direction-dependent mirror/variant masks.
; SpawnHeadingSectors ($9CAE): Small heading choices used when objects spawn near cell edges.
; ObjectSizeVariants ($9CB2): Sprite variants selected from type and projected-size band.
; ArticulatedOffsetX ($9CBA): Signed X offsets for additional articulated sprite pieces.
; ArticulatedOffsetY ($9CC2): Y offsets for additional articulated sprite pieces.
; WeaponSpriteAttributes0 ($9D22): Weapon sprite component attributes indexed by class, state and tick.
; WeaponSpriteX0 ($9D2C): First weapon sprite horizontal offsets.
; WeaponSpriteY0 ($9D36): First weapon sprite vertical offsets relative to aim.
; WeaponSpriteTiles0 ($9D40): Weapon sprite tiles used by both visible components.
; WeaponSpriteAttributes1 ($9D4A): Second weapon sprite component attributes.
; WeaponSpriteX1 ($9D54): Second weapon sprite horizontal offsets.
; WeaponSpriteY1 ($9D5E): Second weapon sprite vertical offsets relative to aim.
; HeadingScaleSamples ($9D68): Packed heading ruler values: low three bits and upper bits feed tick/digit composition.

; Convert three decimal deltas to binary, compute bearing, perspective depth and apparent scale, clip against screen limits, choose a directional sprite and enqueue it. Carry set rejects the object; clear accepts it.
; Divide the retained world magnitude by the angle-derived divisor using sixteen restoring steps. The original projection table generator is unresolved.
; Invert half the depth quotient to obtain apparent scale; apply height/sign and slot-specific offsets, then reject off-screen or excessively close objects.
; Combine object type, size band and desired/current heading into a metasprite variant; special type zero uses its own five-variant layout.
; Types 8/9 at large projected scale replenish resources and request the opening/contact initializer. Exact natural contact routes were not exhaustively exercised.
; Seed the resource counters from the zero-based mission index: increasing ammunition and later-mission stock limits.
; Select a five-byte increment record by mission/4. Add to the five counters with saturation at $FF.
; Three repeated five-byte numeric records, preceding code consumes indexed $A12B,Y; static bounded numeric data. No claim of natural trigger.
; Fixed CPU view $A12B..$A139; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; ResupplyIncrements ($A12B): Three five-byte resource increment records selected by mission/4; addition saturates each counter.
; Increment the appropriate summary counter, decrement remaining objectives and start completion messaging when none remain. Preserve caller X/Y across score and sound work.
; Preserve X/Y and increment score starting at decimal place 6; shared by the contact/hit paths.
; Preserve X/Y and increment score starting at decimal place 5.

; Skip while paused. Scale a signed velocity through a fractional accumulator, then update the selected packed decimal coordinate with wrapping/clamping. Mark the coordinate snapshot dirty after a whole-unit change.
; Software decimal subtraction using MotionOperand and incoming carry. Correct low-nibble borrow and return decimal carry without relying on 6502 decimal mode.
; Software decimal addition using MotionOperand and incoming carry; correct nibble and byte overflow. Shared correction tails also serve the general decimal helpers.
; A minus DecimalOperand minus inverted carry. Save binary flags, correct decimal borrow and return carry for multi-byte subtraction.
; Shared decimal subtraction tail; restore the saved carry before correcting a full-byte borrow.
; A plus DecimalOperand plus carry. Apply low-nibble and byte corrections, returning decimal carry for the next byte.
; Shared addition tail restores saved carry, adds $60 on decimal overflow and returns corrected A/carry.
; Advance the feedback shift register five or eight times according to the simulation tick and return its value, preserving Y.
; Repeated little-endian values and byte runs between supported routines; indexed references near $A2C0 checked. Generic data; precise roles unresolved.
; Fixed CPU view $A2C0..$A2FF; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; AiSequencePrimary ($A2C0): Little-endian callback sequence consumed through CallObjectAi; zero high-byte terminator resets the cursor. Entry contracts support the callback code independently.
; AiSequenceSecondary ($A2C8): Alternate callback sequence with the same cursor/terminator convention.
; ObjectAiNearRangeLo ($A2D4): Type-indexed low decimal range thresholds.
; ObjectAiNearRangeHi ($A2D6): Type-indexed high decimal range thresholds.
; ObjectAiSequenceRoots ($A2D8): Type-indexed little-endian roots for callback sequences.
; HeadingZSignMasks ($A2DC): Quadrant sign masks ORed into the Z velocity magnitude.
; HeadingXSignMasks ($A2DF): Quadrant sign masks ORed into the X velocity magnitude.
; DamageFlashColors ($A2E3): Four random palette flash choices.
; WeaponIndicatorY ($A2E7): Weapon-indexed indicator Y positions.
; MissionAiFireThreshold ($A2EC): Mission-indexed probability threshold for incoming fire.
; MissionAiSpeeds ($A2F6): Mission-indexed desired object speeds.
; Choose a random edge and position, then derive velocity toward the HUD reference point. Edge choice changes sign interpretation.
; Choose a bounded random X at Y=$4C, then aim it toward the reference point. Mission/contact state may choose a special particle tile.
; Eight non-restoring quotient steps approximate the X share of the particle direction vector.
; Eight-byte repeated signed-coordinate pattern between routines. Generic numeric data; no schema claim.
; Fixed CPU view $A3ED..$A3F4; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; ParticleEdgeX ($A3ED): Edge-spawn X values; $80 requests a random coordinate.
; ParticleEdgeY ($A3F1): Edge-spawn Y values; $80 requests a random coordinate.
; Populate OAM for ten particles, eight projectile indicators and two target-relative markers. Inactive entries move to Y=$F0; scene sprites use the separate metasprite builder.
; If enabled, advance tempo and noise, then four channels. Per-note counters drive envelopes and stream advancement; effect-owned channels suppress normal music writes.
; For a channel not owned by an effect, write cached volume/control and low period to its APU register quartet.

; Decrement modulation delay on a tempo tick, fetch the channel's handler pointer and tail-call it through SoundIndirect. Callback contracts establish these entries; pointers alone are not code evidence.

; Seven little-endian handler pointers at $A57D: $A544,$A58E,$A5C1,$A5BD,$A58B,$A5B8,$A607, consumed through sound dispatch $A57A. Static pointer data, not pointer values alone proving target code. A58B/A58E overlapping entry interpretation documented separately.
; Fixed CPU view $A57D..$A58A; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; MusicModulationPointers ($A57D): Seven little-endian modulation callback pointers; two entries use overlapping instruction views at A58B/A58E.
; Entry selects bit shift 4. The encoded BIT at $A58D consumes the alternate LDY #2 bytes at $A58E; both paths converge at $A590. Preserve this overlapping encoding exactly.
; Use shifted vblank time modulo eight to choose duty bits, retaining the cached low six control bits.
; Eight explicit duty-mask constants $80,$C0,$40,$00,$40,$80,$C0,$00 indexed from $A5A3 after AND7. Exact selected domain and code-delimited extent coincide.
; Fixed CPU view $A5B0..$A5B7; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; DutyModulationMasks ($A5B0): Eight duty bits selected with index masked to 0..7; lower control bits are retained.
; Select the alternate signed delta table with an eight-step mask; shares the pitch modulation core.
; Select the primary pitch delta table with an eight-step mask.
; Select the primary pitch delta table with a sixteen-step mask.
; Fetch the note's base low period and add a time-indexed modulation delta. Only the cached low period changes here.

; Repeated signed small-value modulation sequences adjacent to sound update code. Full gap checked against code boundaries and indexed operand bases; data role supported, exact channel interpretation unresolved.
; Fixed CPU view $A5EF..$A606; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; PitchModulationPrimary ($A5EF): Time-indexed signed low-period offsets for the primary modulation path.
; PitchModulationAlternate ($A5FF): Time-indexed low-period offsets for the alternate modulation path.
; Alternate callback entry tail-calls the eight-step pitch modulator.
; Increment the cached volume by a time-indexed delta, saturate at 15, preserve control bits and then apply alternate pitch modulation.
; Eight 01/00 delta values addressed by $A61D after AND7. Independently bounded eight-byte domain and next code entry.
; Fixed CPU view $A62F..$A636; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; VolumeModulationDeltas ($A62F): Eight zero/one increments, with cached volume saturated at 15.
; Noise note $3F is a no-op; other values start the noise effect helper. The stream's noise channel has a distinct shorter interpretation.
; Read duration, note/flags and envelope timing from a three-byte record. Select channel instrument/envelope, manage APU enable bits and write pitch registers unless an effect owns the channel.
; Use the channel instrument index to resolve a little-endian envelope pointer into SoundIndirect.
; Read alternating high/low volume nibbles. $F1 is an envelope control marker that sets a release delay; exhausted envelopes mark their cursor $FF. Triangle uses its own control path.
; Advance three-byte records, loop/repeat on zero duration and consume $FF instrument/modulation records before returning the next note.
; Walk song->sequence->pattern pointer layers. High-byte zero encodes a sequence jump/stop, high-byte one a repeat count; other words identify record streams. Carry set reports song stop.
; A selects the song, X can choose an alternate sequence start through bit 7. Copy four channel roots, clear cursors/counters, disable unowned channels and load tempo.
; Add A to the zero-page word at X, incrementing its high byte on carry. Return the new low byte in A.
; For an active unowned noise channel, write the selected two-byte noise record in reverse countdown order; clear the effect when the cursor expires.
; Load initial noise control/period and its countdown from a four-byte descriptor, restarting APU channel enable as needed.

; Monotonically descending little-endian numeric values followed by zero/one runs between audio routines; checked full 128-byte gap, no conflicting code. Composite generic data, exact musical interpretation unresolved.
; Fixed CPU view $A925..$A9A4; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; NoteTimerWords ($A925): Little-endian APU period values indexed by six-bit note number; high timer bits receive fixed length bits on write.
; Report song activity in carry. At song time major 2 and minor $31 or later, restart song 1 and return A=$80 as the completion cue; other active times return zero.

; Repeated little-endian in-range pointers, zero delimiters, FF/FE command runs, repeated note-like records through code boundary $ACD8. Neighboring audio consumers and full pattern inspected; structured non-code without asserting command schema or natural selection.
; Fixed CPU view $A9C9..$ACD7; source bytes remain in the local image asset.
; NoiseInitialRecords ($A9D7): Four-byte noise descriptors: initial control, period, countdown and retained format byte. Exact musical naming unresolved.
; InstrumentEnvelopePointers ($A9E3): Instrument-indexed little-endian envelope roots.
; InstrumentControlBytes ($A9E7): Instrument-indexed control values used when starting notes.
; InstrumentEnvelopeLengths ($A9E9): Envelope bounds/timing values used by nibble cursors and release setup.
; SongChannelRoots ($A9F1): Eight bytes per song: four little-endian channel roots, followed through sequence/pattern layers.
; SongTempoSteps ($ACD6): Song-indexed tempo accumulator increment immediately before mission initialization code.

; Configure scene sprite bounds and screen/palette tables. A resumed contact transition preserves world state; a new mission clears gameplay RAM, seeds occupancy and resources, and installs MissionFrame.
; Clear the gameplay zero-page range and RAM $03D5..$06C4, preserving mission/score state according to the initialization sentinel.
; Create ten particles, then override their starting positions from fixed tables for a repeatable initial display.

; Load terminated (cell value,index) pairs, then add two randomized populations subject to empty-cell/type/count restrictions. The retry loops are bounded by valid mission table assumptions, not a fixed iteration counter.
; Seed player decimal position, active flags and heading, resources, HUD OAM and palette. Set the main frame callback to MissionFrame.
; For each effect-owned channel, decrement its duration and invoke the descriptor's callback. Expired channels are disabled and released back to music.
; Indirect sound callback trampoline. X is channel, Y=4*channel, A=remaining duration; callers explicitly establish this contract.
; X is an eight-byte effect descriptor index. Carry-derived policy may restart an identical effect; choose its channel, set duration/ownership and copy nonzero APU initialization bytes.
; Preserve A/X/Y and carry restart policy, then request descriptor 0.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 1.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 2; commonly used for impact feedback.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 3; used by several firing/flash paths.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 4.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 5; used at damage warning thresholds.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 6.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 7.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 8; used by the shake/palette response.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 9; used by object destruction.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 10.
; Preserve registers and request effect descriptor 11; used by text/alert updates.
; When music is absent ensure the continuous channel effect is active; while music owns the scene, release only its matching effect.
; Keep duration alive, alternate pulse volume/duty with vblank time and write the cached continuous-sound period.
; Derive high timer and volume fields from the remaining duration for the callback's APU quartet.
; Use a bright cyclic attack above duration $30, then reduce volume in four-tick steps with period low $FE.
; Use a cyclic attack above duration $30, then reduce volume in four-tick steps with period low $FF.
; Use duration low bits for timer high and middle bits for pulse control.
; Duration bit 5 gates a loud low-period sweep versus silent control value $30.
; Map duration/4 into the low volume nibble, retaining fixed pulse control bits.
; Keep duration alive and alternate fixed pulse control with the current spatial volume on the vblank divider.

; Twelve complete eight-byte records bounded by $B0AC and next accepted handler $B10C. AF7E applies first four APU register bytes; AF16 reads final callback word at record+6; middle fields used by AF41/AF69. All record callback contracts checked. ; Four immutable 8 KiB CHR banks; each bank has 512 NES 2bpp tiles (16 bytes/tile).
